indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the word serial are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A television serial set in the ancient biblical city of Jericho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to rearrange SERIAL; the whole word is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Jericho is an ancient city in the Holy Land, the biblical country of the Hebrews.

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: Nobody joining in is rude or unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'No-one' looks like a single pronoun, but it splits into NO and 'one', which is I.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome describes something nasty or disgusting, especially a smell, so it is a synonym for offensive.

parts.note: orange is a colour, so something coloured can be orange
a man is a person

explanation.surface: A coloured person who supported a king called William.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Orange won the Battle of the Boyne in 1690; Orangemen, members of a Protestant order in Northern Ireland, march in his memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order honour and stood behind King William III, William of Orange.

explanation.surface: Declining to merge a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as RE-FUSE, with a different pronunciation from the verb meaning decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to say no to something; to fuse again, split as re-fuse, is to merge a second time.

explanation.surface: Paying later in exchange for getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: Access was a popular credit card in Britain from 1972 to 1996, so the first definition is a brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: Access was a British credit card, a form of deferred payment; entree means the right of entry.

clue.text: Small bill the clerical assistant should find correct

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation of account, a bill, so it is a small one
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest

explanation.surface: A small invoice that a junior clergyman should find in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means exact and free from error, a synonym of correct.

clue.text: A water-course may upset the French

parts.note: can and may both express being permitted or able

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in a down clue the words for the French are turned upside down

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A stream might overturn some French people.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the French article reads bottom to top, giving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway, a man-made water-course.

clue.text: Still only for the male worker around the North

indicators.note: around means the stag and worker pair are placed either side of the north abbreviation

parts.note: a stag party or night is for men only
an ant is the classic worker insect
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A men-only event with a worker somewhere up north, calm and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a men-only celebration before a wedding; 'around' puts the stag and the worker on either side of the north abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is motionless, not flowing, so it is still.

clue.text: Beats using craft about business drive!

indicators.note: about means the craft letters are placed around the other pieces

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
urge means drive or impulse

explanation.surface: A boat used for some commercial push, with a punishing exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the steamship letters around the company and drive words; the exclamation mark is surface decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to whip or flog, so scourges means beats.

indicators.note: badly-behaved means unruly, so these letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unruly young men can disgrace themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly-behaved' tells you to rearrange LADS and CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an occasion of public disgrace, so it means shame.

clue.text: Crime committed by a minister losing his head

indicators.note: losing his head means the minister word drops its first letter

parts.note: a parson is a minister of the church

explanation.surface: An offence carried out by a beheaded clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' takes the P off PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the deliberate setting of fire to property, a criminal offence.

indicators.note: out side reads as outside, so the throw word wraps around the pastry word

parts.note: to sling is to throw
a tart is a pastry

explanation.surface: Pastry gets hurled out to one side, surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out side' is printed as two words but means outside: the throw word goes around the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising or alarming, a synonym of shocking.

explanation.surface: Putting someone in court and going through it.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses use the same verb: putting an accused before a court, and having a go at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge may hear a case and test it in court; to undergo or sample something is also this verb.

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange palm growing in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' tells you to rearrange PALM and TREE. Lampeter is a small university town in west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampeter is a market town in Ceredigion, so it is a place in Wales.

explanation.surface: Educational establishments and getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to coach or teach them; railway carriages pulled by an engine are a means of travel.

parts.note: to ration is to limit use, conserving supplies
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A sound reason to save beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or justification behind something, its basis.

clue.text: The writer lies about after a fine

indicators.note: after means the rearranged lies follow the letter from a

parts.note: a pen is what a writer uses, standing for the writer

indicators.note: about means the letters of lies are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author tells untruths after a monetary penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer stands for the tool a writer uses. 'about' rearranges the letters of the word lies, and 'after' puts that result behind the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine someone is to punish them with a monetary charge, so it means to impose a penalty.

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, the church

explanation.surface: Bending low inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow is a curved shape, as is an arc, a segment of a curve.

parts.note: the rest means the others
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: Self-control displayed while everyone else falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep in check, which is to control.

clue.text: The main part of a ploughman's lunch is cheese and bread

indicators.note: part of means the letters are a piece taken from inside the words cheese and

explanation.surface: A ploughman's lunch consists mostly of cheese and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like 'the main part', but it is the definition: the main is an old word for the open ocean. A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetic and old usage the main means the high seas, the open ocean.

clue.text: Catty, so gets nothing back in remuneration

indicators.note: in means the reversed nothing goes inside the payment word

parts.note: a fee is a payment for work

indicators.note: back means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Being spiteful, someone gets nothing in return for their pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NIL into LIN, which goes 'in' FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feline means cat-like, and catty literally describes cats.

parts.note: F is a musical note

explanation.surface: Write it down carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit and well both mean healthy, in good condition.

clue.text: The vehicle I own is bright red

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
what I own is mine

explanation.surface: My car is a vivid red.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson pigment, a shade of red.

clue.text: One maybe meant it to be confidential

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: maybe suggests an alternative arrangement of these letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone perhaps intended a matter to be kept private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the two words into NTIMATE, which follows the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate details are private and personal, so they are confidential.

clue.text: Settled for a good man in distress

indicators.note: in means the good man abbreviation goes inside the distress word

parts.note: need means hardship or distress
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man in trouble finds a home.
explanation.walkthrough: ST, for saint, is a crossword stock for 'good man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that have nested have settled into a home.

clue.text: Most senior set led to effect re form

indicators.note: to effect reform means to make changes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The oldest group was in charge of bringing about change.
explanation.walkthrough: 're form' is printed split, giving reform; it tells you to rearrange SET LED.
explanation.definitionFit: The eldest child is the oldest, the most senior in age.

clue.text: Beat a friend hollow and scoffed

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a pit is a hollow in the ground
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: Thrash a mate thoroughly and mock them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat a friend hollow' reads as a thrashing, but 'hollow' is a noun here and 'scoffed' means eaten, not jeered.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart that palpitates throbs or pounds, so it beats.

clue.text: Force a one penny increase in pay

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
a rise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: Pushing for a one-penny pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something is to lever it open by force.

parts.note: taken as written
mad means demented

explanation.surface: A wanderer who is not at all deranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad travels from place to place with no fixed home, a wandering person.

explanation.surface: Two words for things that match.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar means alike, resembling something; it also means matching in character or analogous.

indicators.note: to make means the letters of the first word are used to make another word

explanation.surface: Permitted to produce banners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' tells you to rearrange LICENSED. 'flags' looks like a noun, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that flags weakens or droops, and a thing that weakens is said to fall away in strength.

clue.text: Running water is always provided in quarters

indicators.note: provided in means the always word is put inside the quarters

parts.note: S and N, south and north, are compass quarters
ever means always

explanation.surface: Housing that always has running water laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a body of flowing water, and the Severn is a well-known one.
